narrative:
The model predicted an 82.8% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is so high, the admissions system automatically rejected your law school application.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors, ranked by importance. Your first-year and third-year class rankings were the strongest reasons for the negative outcome. Being in the bottom decile for grades in both Year 1 and Year 3 pushed the prediction heavily toward failure. These early academic standings mattered more than any other information in your file. Your LSAT score was the third most influential factor and also pulled the prediction toward failure.

Taken together, your low class rankings and modest LSAT result told the model you were likely to struggle with the bar exam. Other details such as your undergraduate GPA of 2.9, upper-middle family income, and plan to attend full-time had far less impact.

You should focus on strengthening the areas the model weighed most heavily. Consider retaking the LSAT to raise your score, enrolling in academic support programs, or gaining additional legal experience before reapplying. These steps can directly address the specific concerns that led to your rejection. (198 words)
